title: Hyaluronic-Acid Based Hydrogels for 3-Dimensional Culture of Patient-Derived Glioblastoma Cells
protocol: Dissolve 500 mg of sodium hyaluronate in deionized, distilled water to make a 10 mg/mL solution in an autoclave-sterilized Erlenmeyer flask.
Stir the hyaluronic acid solution at room temperature for 2 hours at approximately 200 rpm.
Adjust the pH of the HA solution to 5.5 using 0.1 M hydrochloric acid.
Dissolve 69.6 mg of 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC) in 1 mL of deionized, distilled water and add the EDC solution to the HA solution.
Add 17.9 mg of N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) to the reaction mixture.
Adjust the pH of the reaction solution to 5.5 using 0.1 M HCl and incubate at room temperature for 45 minutes.
Dissolve 70.0 mg of cystamine dihydrochloride in 1 mL of deionized, distilled water and add it to the reaction mixture.
Adjust the pH of the solution to 6.25 using 0.1 M sodium hydroxide.
Incubate the reaction at room temperature overnight while stirring.
Adjust the pH of the reaction solution to around 8 using 1 M NaOH.
Add 192 mg of dithiothreitol (DTT) at a 4x molar ratio to the reaction.
Adjust the pH back to 8 after adding DTT and stir for 1-2 hours at room temperature.
Use 1 M HCl to adjust the pH of the solution to 4.
Transfer the entire reaction mixture into pre-soaked dialysis membrane (molecular weight cut-off around 13 kDa).
Dialyze against DiH2O pre-adjusted to pH 4, with a volume at least 40 times that of the reacted HA solution.
Replace the dialysis solution twice daily for 3 days at room temperature.
Filter the dialyzed solution through a 0.22 µm membrane using a vacuum-driven filter.
Flash freeze the thiolated HA solution in liquid nitrogen.
Use a lyophilizer to freeze dry samples over 2 days.
Store thiolated HA in dry form in a vacuum-sealed desiccator at -20 °C for at least 6 months.
Determine the degree of thiolation using Ellman's test and/or proton NMR spectroscopy.
Dissolve thiolated HA at the desired concentration (13.3 mg/mL) in HEPES-buffered saline in an amber vial to minimize light exposure.
Keep the solution stirring constantly during preparation.
Dissolve thiolated hyaluronic acid within 2 hours in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) at pH 7.4 below 15 mg/mL concentration.
Prepare 50 mg/mL PEG-Mal and PEG-thiol stock solutions by dissolving them in PBS, pH 7.4.
Dissolve cysteine-containing peptides in PBS to prepare a stock solution with a concentration of 2-4 mM.
Soak silicone rubber molds in ethanol for at least 20 min to clean them.
Autoclave cleaned silicone rubber molds for sterilization.
Mix PEG-Mal and thiolated hyaluronic acid solutions according to desired recipe concentrations.
Add cysteine-containing peptides to the mixture if incorporating into hydrogels as negative controls or integrin-binding peptide RGD.
Encapsulate 500,000 cells/mL patient-derived GBM cells in prepared hydrogel mixtures.
Dilute PEG-Mal stock solution (50 mg/mL) to 12.5 mg/mL by adding 40 µL of the stock solution to 120 µL PBS.
Split the diluted solution into two 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, with each tube containing 80 µL.
Add 16 µL of stock RGD solution (2.8 mM) to one tube.
Add 16 µL of stock cysteine solution (2.8 mM) to the second tube.
Vortex to mix both solutions.
Place the PEG-Mal-RGD and PEG-Mal-CYS solutions on ice until use.
Dilute the PEG-thiol stock solution (50 mg/mL) to 5 mg/mL by mixing 4 µL of 50 mg/mL stock solution with 36 µL of PBS.
Add 120 µL of dissolved, thiolated HA from step 2.1 to the diluted PEG-thiol solution.
Pipette slowly to avoid solution sticking to the walls of micropipette tip and to improve measurement accuracy.
Place clean, dry molds into each well of a non-tissue culture treated 12-well plate.
Press the gel mold using the clean, blunt end of a pipette tip.
Centrifuge gliomaspheres at 500 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of cell dissociation enzyme to the cell pellet.
Incubate for 5 min, gently tapping the tube to agitate.
Add 4 mL of complete culture medium (50 ng/mL EGF, 20 ng/mL FGF-2, 25 µg/mL heparin, G21 supplement and 1% penicillin/streptomycin in DMEM/F12) to the cells.
Centrifuge again at 500 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of complete medium.
Pass suspended cells through a 70 µm cell strainer.
Wash the strainer with an additional 4 mL of complete medium to maximize the number of cells recovered.
Estimate the concentration of cells in the suspension using a hemocytometer.
Split the cell suspension into 2 centrifuge tubes, each containing ~80,000 cells.
Centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend one pellet in 80 µL of PEG-MAL-RGD solution.
Resuspend a second pellet in 80 µL of PEG-MAL-CYS solution.
Dispense 40 µL of HA solution into each rubber silicone mold using a 200 µL, wide-orifice micropipette tip.
Mix the 40 µL of PEG-MAL-CYS or PEG-MAL-RGD cell solution with the HA solution in the mold.
Pipette up and down quickly no more than 10 times to ensure even mixing.
Keep the tip below liquid level to avoid formation of air bubbles.
Place the well-plate containing gel-encapsulated cells into a 37 °C cell culture incubator for 5-10 minutes.
Add 2-2.5 mL of culture medium to each well with formed gels.
Gently separate the mold and gel using a sterile, 2 µL pipette tip or micro-spatula.
Remove the mold from the well plate using pre-sterilized forceps.
Place the well plate back into the cell incubator (37 °C and 5% CO2) for culture and future experiments.
Replace medium in gel cultures every 3-4 days, taking care not to aspirate hydrogels when removing medium.
If bioluminescence imaging is planned, add 1 mM of D-luciferin to the culture medium 1 h prior to luminescence imaging.
Chill 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes on ice (1 per gel sample).
Cool centrifuge to 4 °C.
Remove medium from well plates.
Transfer gels into prechilled microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 100 µL of RIPA buffer with 1x protease/phosphatase inhibitors.
Break up the gel by pushing the whole mixture through a 20 G needle at least 20 times using a 1 mL syringe.
Flash spin the sample using a bench top microcentrifuge and place the sample back on ice.
Vortex samples briefly every 5 min for a total of 20 min.
Centrifuge samples at 14000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to new, pre-chilled microcentrifuge tubes.
Store supernatant at -20°C (short-term) or and -80°C (long-term).
Perform gel electrophoresis using standard procedures.
Remove medium from the gel culture.
Transfer the gel culture into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate gel with 500 µL of cell dissociation enzyme at 37 °C for 5 min, occasionally flicking the tube to agitate.
Transfer the mixture into a 50 mL centrifuge tube with 5 mL of complete medium.
Place the tube on ice.
Attach a 20G needle onto a 10 mL syringe.
Gently pull the cell suspension up and down through the needle 8 times.
Flow the mixture through 70 µm cell strainer into a new 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Apply an additional 5 mL of complete medium through the strainer to collect any remaining cells.
Centrifuge the sample at 400 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in desired buffer for flow cytometry.
Remove medium from gel cultures.
Incubate gel cultures with 2 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) at 4 °C overnight.
Remove PFA from gels.
Add 2 mL of 5% sucrose in PBS to gels.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Replace the 5% sucrose solution with 2 mL of 20% sucrose in PBS.
Incubate for 30 min.
Replace the sucrose solution again with 2 mL of fresh 20% sucrose in PBS.
Incubate for an additional 30 min.
Repeat replacement of the sucrose solution with 2 mL of fresh 20% sucrose in PBS.
Incubate at 4 °C overnight.
Prepare 20% sucrose in Optimal Cutting Temperature (OCT) compound.
Remove the 20% sucrose solution from gels.
Gently pour 20% sucrose in OCT solution over the gel to cover entirely.
Incubate at 4 °C for 3 h.
Transfer the gel into the center of an embedding mold carefully using a large, flat spatula.
Cool 2-methylbutane inside a cryochamber with dry ice.
Fill the embedding mold with pure OCT up to just below its top edge.
Freeze the hydrogel sample by immersing it in cooled 2-methylbutane.
Proceed to sectioning of the sample using a cryostat.
Section the sample at thicknesses between 10-18 µm and around -26 °C temperature.
Perform standard immunostaining procedures on sectioned gel culture.
Remove the culture medium from hydrogel cultures.
Transfer the hydrogel culture into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using a P1000 transfer pipette with wide-bore tip.
Add 350 μL of buffer RLT to the hydrogel culture in the tube.
Shred the gel by pushing the mixture through a 20 G needle attached to a 1 mL syringe at least 20 times.
Transfer the whole mixture into a homogenizer column placed in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 13,000 x g for 2 min.
Transfer the supernatant into a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube carefully.
Mix the lysate sample with 350 μL of 100% ethanol.
Transfer all the sample to a spin column from the kit and place it in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge for 1 min at 13,000 x g.
